title: A directed inverse system of nonempty constructible-closed subsets of spectral spaces has a compatible family of points
statement: Let $K$ be a directed set (nonempty, any two elements have a common upper bound), let $(Y_k)_{k\in K}$ be spectral spaces [def-weil-spectral-space] and for $k\le k'$ let $g_{kk'}:Y_{k'}\to Y_k$ be spectral maps (continuous, with $g_{kk'}^{-1}(W)$ quasi-compact for every quasi-compact open $W\subseteq Y_k$), with $g_{kk}=\mathrm{id}$ and $g_{kk'}\circ g_{k'k''}=g_{kk''}$ for $k\le k'\le k''$. For every $k\in K$ let $Z_k\subseteq Y_k$ be a nonempty subset which is closed in the constructible topology of $Y_k$ [def-weil-pbc-constructible-topology] (the topology on $Y_k$ with subbase the quasi-compact open subsets of $Y_k$ and their complements), and assume $g_{kk'}(Z_{k'})\subseteq Z_k$ for all $k\le k'$. Then there is a family $(z_k)_{k\in K}$ with $z_k\in Z_k$ for every $k$ and $g_{kk'}(z_{k'})=z_k$ for all $k\le k'$.

source.place: Topology, Lemma Tag 0A2W (label lemma-inverse-limit-spectral-spaces-nonempty, line 4810), part (1), stated there for a cofiltered index category; a directed set $K$ (the category with one arrow $k'\to k$ for $k\le k'$) is the special case used here. Stacks' proof uses Lemma Tag 0901 (lemma-constructible-hausdorff-quasi-compact, line 4305: the constructible topology of a spectral space is Hausdorff and quasi-compact) and Lemma Tag 0A2R (lemma-nonempty-limit, line 2507: a cofiltered limit of nonempty quasi-compact Hausdorff spaces is nonempty)

proof.text: *Step 1 (the spaces $Z'_k$).* For $k\in K$ let $Y'_k$ be the set $Y_k$ with its constructible topology [def-weil-pbc-constructible-topology] and $Z'_k$ the set $Z_k$ with the subspace topology from $Y'_k$ [def-kun-subspace-topology]. $Y'_k$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-spectral-constructible-topology-quasi-compact] ($Y_k$ is spectral) and $Z_k$ is closed in $Y'_k$ by hypothesis, so $Z'_k$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-in-quasi-compact]. $Y'_k$ is Hausdorff by [lem-weil-pbc-spectral-constructible-topology-hausdorff]; hence so is its subspace $Z'_k$: two distinct points of $Z_k$ have disjoint open neighbourhoods $A,B$ in $Y'_k$, and $A\cap Z_k$, $B\cap Z_k$ are disjoint open neighbourhoods in $Z'_k$. Finally $Z'_k\ne\emptyset$ by hypothesis.

source.place: Topology, Lemma Tag 0A2W (lemma-inverse-limit-spectral-spaces-nonempty, line 4810), proof, part (1)

proof.text: *Step 2 (the transition maps).* Let $k\le k'$. Since $g_{kk'}:Y_{k'}\to Y_k$ is a spectral map of spectral spaces, it is continuous as a map $Y'_{k'}\to Y'_k$ by [lem-weil-pbc-spectral-map-constructible-continuous]. As $g_{kk'}(Z_{k'})\subseteq Z_k$, it restricts to a map $h_{kk'}:Z'_{k'}\to Z'_k$, $z\mapsto g_{kk'}(z)$, which is continuous for the subspace topologies [def-kun-subspace-topology]: for $A\subseteq Y'_k$ open, $h_{kk'}^{-1}(A\cap Z_k)=g_{kk'}^{-1}(A)\cap Z_{k'}$ is open in $Z'_{k'}$. The identities $g_{kk}=\mathrm{id}$ and $g_{kk'}\circ g_{k'k''}=g_{kk''}$ restrict to $h_{kk}=\mathrm{id}$ and $h_{kk'}\circ h_{k'k''}=h_{kk''}$ for $k\le k'\le k''$.

source.place: Topology, Lemma Tag 0A2W (lemma-inverse-limit-spectral-spaces-nonempty, line 4810), proof, part (1)

proof.text: *Step 3 (conclusion).* $K$ is a preordered set in which any two elements have a common upper bound, and by Steps 1 and 2 $(Z'_k,h_{kk'})$ is an inverse system over $K$ of nonempty quasi-compact Hausdorff spaces with continuous transition maps satisfying $h_{kk}=\mathrm{id}$ and $h_{kk'}\circ h_{k'k''}=h_{kk''}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-directed-limit-compact-hausdorff-nonempty] there is a family $(z_k)_{k\in K}$ with $z_k\in Z'_k$ and $h_{kk'}(z_{k'})=z_k$ for $k\le k'$. As sets $Z'_k=Z_k$ and $h_{kk'}(z_{k'})=g_{kk'}(z_{k'})$, so $z_k\in Z_k$ and $g_{kk'}(z_{k'})=z_k$ for all $k\le k'$ (Stacks: '$\lim Z'_i=\lim Z_i$ as sets').
